column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah the Exalted said: Whoever is hostile to an ally (walī) of Mine, I have declared war against him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory on him,

and My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him. When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him; and if he seeks refuge with Me, I will surely grant him refuge.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.

His words, “Whoever is hostile to an ally of Mine, I have declared war against him”: this hadith is one of the ḥadīth qudsī that the Messenger ﷺ relates from his Lord. Al-Shawkānī devoted to its explanation a book he named Qaṭr al-Walī bi-Sharḥ Ḥadīth al-Walī.
The allies (awliyāʾ) of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are the God-fearing believers, as the Exalted said:

“Unquestionably, the allies of Allah—there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve: those who believed and were fearing Allah” [Yūnus 10:62–63]. The meaning of “I have declared war against him” is: I have informed him that I am at war with him. It shows the danger of being hostile to the allies of Allah, and that it is one of the major sins.

His words, “My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory on him”: this sentence and what follows make clear that the alliance (walāyah) of Allah is attained only by drawing near to Him through performing the obligations
and doing voluntary deeds in addition. It shows that drawing near through performing the obligations is more beloved to Allah than voluntary deeds,

because in that lies doing what Allah has made obligatory and leaving what Allah has made unlawful. The one who does the obligations and leaves the unlawful takes the middle course (muqtaṣid), and the one who does them and does voluntary deeds along with them is foremost in good deeds.

His words, “and My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him…” to the end: voluntary deeds are doing righteous deeds in addition to the obligations. Doing them and persevering in them brings the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; and when he attains that love, he gains Allah's guidance in his conduct,

so he hears only what is right, sees only what is right, takes only what is right and walks only to what is right; and Allah honours him by answering his supplication when he calls on Him and granting him refuge from what he seeks refuge from.
An explanation of the virtue of the allies of Allah and of how dangerous it is to be hostile to them.
The alliance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is attained by performing the obligations and doing voluntary deeds.
The most beloved means of drawing near to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is performing the obligations.
Affirmation of the attribute of love for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Deeds differ in how beloved they are to Allah.
Doing voluntary deeds after performing the obligations brings the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Whoever gains the love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, He guides him in his hearing, his sight, his striking and his walking.
The love of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, brings the servant the answering of his supplication and refuge from what he fears.
Allah's reward to the servant, the Mighty and Majestic, is in granting what he seeks and keeping him safe from what he dreads.
